gold: Early state (Session 2): Marcus describes a menu with multiple elaborate courses — roast squash, heritage tomatoes, slow-braised lamb, a fig dessert — each component carefully chosen and seasonally sourced. The phrase 'I think they're right' confirms this was not just external pressure but internal recognition. New state (Session 7): 'I launched the new menu Friday. Five courses instead of nine, simpler sourcing, fewer components on each plate.' A customer returning the following night for a second portion of chicken becomes his new benchmark: 'That one thing told me more than any review.'

**What it became (Session 7 / the Oct 13 exchange):** he launched a new menu — five courses instead of nine, simpler sourcing, fewer components on each plate — aiming for “simple food that people actually want to come back for” and “honest food for people I actually care about.” The proof for him was a customer who returned the next night and asked for a second portion of the chicken: “That one thing told me more than any review.” He later reports the restaurant had its best two weeks since opening.
